While we don't know if Walt-the-Dentist was in on it or not, it's the baiting of Cecil that disturbs me most.

I saw similar tactics used in Colorado to bag bear, who are creatures of habit.

For five or six months leading up to the legal hunting season various town layabouts would make the rounds of area restaurants, begging for scraps and throwing them into 55 gallon drums roped to the back of their pick ups. When full enough they'd drive up into a wilderness area, drag the can in as far as they could, dump it, then grab binoculars and start monitoring the site.

Once a bear found the leavings the battle was half over. Now it was just a matter of collect more, dump, check for sign, lather-rinse-and-repeat until about a week before the season started. The bear? He'd come back for weeks, looking to see if any more free lunch had arrived.

Meanwhile, our friendly bear baiter would take out an ad in the local paper, touting themselves as a "guide" and there was never a shortage of out of state hunters willing to part with a semi-princely sum for a "guaranteed kill".

You know the rest of the story.

So yeah, for me it the baiting that's the most repugnant aspect of this story and the one thing that says Walt isn't the hunter, or sportsman, he thinks he is.
